Title: Optimizing the performance of vehicular delay tolerant networks using multi-objective PSO and artificial intelligence
authors: Vishakha Chourasia, Sudhakar Pandey, Sanjay Kumar
network_environment: Vehicular Delay Tolerant Network (VDTN) in an urban scenario (Helsinki city map)
swarm_algorithm: Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO)
agent_characteristics: Offline swarm optimization in MATLAB coupled with ONE simulator; particles represent 5-dimensional weight vectors for social parameters used in distributed forwarding
operational_action: Routing / Opportunistic packet forwarding optimization (optimizing weight coefficients of social attributes to compute next-hop forwarding probability)
handling_of_disconnections: Store-carry-forward (SCF) mechanism where vehicles buffer messages until an opportunistic encounter with a suitable intermediate or destination node occurs
key_metrics_and_results: Optimized delivery ratio (max 0.5584), latency/delay (min 950.32 s), and overhead ratio (min 35.10). Outperformed Epidemic, PRoPHET, and MaxProp protocols, confirmed by Friedman and Nemenyi non-parametric statistical tests.
limitations: The MOPSO optimization framework operates offline; evaluated using simulated synthetic mobility without storage/buffer constraints.
full_citation: [1]V. Chourasia, S. Pandey, and S. Kumar, âOptimizing the performance of vehicular delay tolerant networks using multi-objective PSO and artificial intelligence,â Computer Communications, vol. 177, pp. 10â23, Sep. 2021, doi: 10.1016/j.comcom.2021.06.006.

Title: Transformation from IoT to IoV for waste management in smart cities
authors: Gerald K. Ijemaru, Li Minn Ang, Kah Phooi Seng
network_environment: Opportunistic Vehicular Edge / Internet of Vehicles (IoV) collecting data from Large-Scale Wireless Sensor Networks (LS-WSNs) in smart cities
swarm_algorithm: Ant Colony Optimization routing (specifically Flooded Forward Ant Routing [FFR] and MCBR-AST)
agent_characteristics: Distributed edge nodes consisting of battery-powered sensing smart bins and mobile data collectors (vehicles like buses, taxis, cars) acting as relay agents
operational_action: Opportunistic data collection and multi-hop routing
handling_of_disconnections: Employs delay-tolerant opportunistic store-carry-and-forward via mobile data collectors (MDCs/MULEs) and swarm-based dynamic link estimation probabilities to adapt to dynamic network topology changes
key_metrics_and_results: Evaluated packet delivery ratio (PDR), throughput, latency, energy consumption, and energy efficiency. Swarm algorithms (FFR: 95% PDR, AST: 90% PDR) substantially outperformed classical AODV (45.98% PDR) and CFR (57.0% PDR) while reducing energy consumption significantly.
limitations: Simulations were conducted in a constrained 160m x 160m synthetic grid in RMASE/PROWLER rather than full-scale urban city traces; inherent high latency in opportunistic MDCs.
full_citation: [1]G. K. Ijemaru, L. M. Ang, and K. P. Seng, âTransformation from IoT to IoV for waste management in smart cities,â Journal of Network and Computer Applications, vol. 204, p. 103393, Aug. 2022, doi: 10.1016/j.jnca.2022.103393.

Title: Energy efficient resource allocation algorithms combining PSO with FLC and Taguchi method in hybrid opportunistic networks
authors: Young-Long Chen, Yan-Hao Lin, Hsin-Yu Chen, Kai-Chun Hung
network_environment: Hybrid opportunistic mobile edge network (dual-radio Wi-Fi and LTE-A cellular)
swarm_algorithm: Particle Swarm Optimization combined with Fuzzy Logic Control and Taguchi method (PSO-FLC-TA)
agent_characteristics: Mobile device nodes acting as particles optimizing cluster head selection based on residual energy and communication quality
operational_action: Cluster head selection, multi-hop cluster formation/routing, and QoS-aware priority weighted resource allocation (PWRR/PWRC)
handling_of_disconnections: Cluster reorganization via invitation, join, status, and dismiss control messages; data packet buffering at mobile devices when transmission resources are insufficient
key_metrics_and_results: Prolonged network lifetime (first node depletion delayed to round 210 vs round 120 in DRONEE-W), increased average throughput up to 89.71 Mbps (5.58% increase), reduced average buffer size by 24.29%, and reduced average delay time by 64.6% (down to 2.0648 s)
limitations: Evaluated in a small simulation setup (30 fixed randomly deployed nodes in a 200x200 m area); high physical device mobility and dynamic movement patterns are not explicitly tested
full_citation: [1]Y.-L. Chen, Y.-H. Lin, H.-Y. Chen, and K.-C. Hung, âEnergy efficient resource allocation algorithms combining PSO with FLC and Taguchi method in hybrid opportunistic networks,â Applied Soft Computing, vol. 148, p. 110717, Nov. 2023, doi: 10.1016/j.asoc.2023.110717.

Title: Enhanced UAV-aided vehicular delay tolerant network (VDTN) routing for urban environment using a bio-inspired approach
authors: Youcef Azzoug, Abdelmadjid Boukra
network_environment: UAV-aided Vehicular Delay Tolerant Networks (UVDTNs) in sparse urban environments
swarm_algorithm: Social Spider Optimization (SSO) adapted to evaluate next-hop relay fitness using female spider vibration/attraction models based on historical SCF forwarding factors and geographic distance ratios
agent_characteristics: Distributed execution across edge nodes (ground vehicles and UAVs) upon opportunistic contact encounters
operational_action: Opportunistic Store-Carry-and-Forward (SCF) routing and relay node selection across V2V, V2U, U2V, and U2U links
handling_of_disconnections: Opportunistic Store-Carry-and-Forward (SCF) with dynamic multi-copy exploration phase and restricted single-copy local-search phase
key_metrics_and_results: Evaluated average delivery delay, delivery probability, bundle relay cost, and overhead ratio. Spider-UVDR achieved higher delivery probability (up to ~95%) and significantly reduced relay cost and overhead compared to benchmark protocols (UAV-VDTN, UADD, GSaR, LDAOR, GeoVDM).
limitations: Performance degrades in extremely sparse scenarios and high bundle generation rates due to historical data starvation and node re-selection; assumes UAVs have unlimited energy via solar harvesters.

Title: CONTEXT-NET: A context-aware nexus-based aggregation protocol for opportunistic networks
authors: Rounak Raman, Ayush Yadav, Deepika Kukreja, Deepak Kumar Sharma
network_environment: Opportunistic IoT networks / Delay Tolerant Networks with mobile edge devices, data keepers, and central core

agent_characteristics: Heterogeneous architecture comprising distributed IoT edge nodes, mobile data keepers acting as ferries, and a dynamically elected core super-node

operational_action: Routing and sensor node selection for opportunistic data collection and query-response data transmission
handling_of_disconnections: Store-carry-and-forward mechanism using Exponential Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) where mobile nanonodes buffer/aggregate readings until a physical layer interaction hit (direct contact) occurs with a Nano Router

Title: A Novel Trusted Intelligent Computing-aware Routing Service Offloading Method Based on MOPSO for Internet of Vehicles
authors: Huiyong LI, Furong WANG
network_environment: Computing-aware Internet of Vehicles (IoV) / Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) with device-edge-cloud collaboration

Title: Hybrid Swarm-Based Geographic VDTN Routing
authors: Youcef Azzoug, Abdelmadjid Boukra, Vasco N. G. J. Soares
network_environment: Vehicular Delay Tolerant Network (VDTN)
swarm_algorithm: Firefly Algorithm (FA) combined with Reliable Estimated Time of Delivery (RETD) metric

Title: A Bee Colony-Based Algorithm for Task Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing
authors: Alisson Barbosa de Souza, Paulo Antonio Leal Rego, Vinay Chamola, Tiago Carneiro, Paulo Henrique Gonçalves Rocha, José Neuman de Souza
network_environment: Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) with intermittent connectivity, utilizing heterogeneous V2V (WAVE / IEEE 802.11p) and V2I (5G mmWave) communications across highway and urban settings.
swarm_algorithm: Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) metaheuristic customized as BTV (Bee colony-based Task offloading in Vehicular edge computing), featuring employed, onlooker, and scout bee search phases with constraint feasibility checks.
agent_characteristics: Lightweight decision-making executed locally on the client vehicle, discovering and coordinating candidate vehicular edge nodes and base-station-coupled edge servers via context beacons.
operational_action: Task offloading and scheduling (assigning independent workload tasks across local CPU, neighboring vehicle servers, and fixed 5G edge servers).
handling_of_disconnections: Incorporates predicted link lifetime constraints into feasibility checks; implements a timeout-based failure recovery mechanism where the client monitors beacon messages and executes local backups of tasks if connectivity is lost.
key_metrics_and_results: Achieved up to 74.4% reduction in average application execution time compared to local execution (and outperformed baselines in 97.2% of test cases) while maintaining 0.0% offloading failures and zero energy constraint violations.
limitations: Assumes independent/asynchronous tasks without inter-task precedence or DAG dependencies; decision execution takes up to 100 ms which may become overhead for ultra-strict sub-millisecond control loops; requires the client vehicle to support simultaneous dual wireless interfaces (WAVE and 5G).

Title: A Novel Mobility-Aware Offloading Management Scheme in Sustainable Multi-Access Edge Computing
authors: Shichao Guan, Azzedine Boukerche
network_environment: Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) with mobile User Equipment (UEs) subject to intermittent cloudlet connectivity
swarm_algorithm: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) formulated with a 3D position space (cloudlet resource ID, task type, priority class) and penalty-based fitness function
agent_characteristics: Centralized execution at the regional Cloudlet decision engine for scheduling offloading requests from covered UEs
operational_action: Task offloading scheduling, priority assignment, and computing resource allocation within an M/G/1 queue alongside inter-cloudlet migration
handling_of_disconnections: Predicts UE contact duration using the SMOOTH mobility model to truncate effective task deadlines; tasks that cannot finish before contact loss are either dropped/executed locally on the UE or migrated to neighbor cloudlets/remote Cloud
key_metrics_and_results: Evaluated execution time, UE energy consumption (processing, transmission, idle), fitness value, and task drop/denial-of-service ratio. PSO-based model outperformed Min-Min, Min-Max, and Deadline-greedy in efficiency and reduced task drop rate up to 92.07% vs. priority-based and 66.7% vs. distance-based schemes.
limitations: Assumes Poisson task arrivals and exponential service times which may not capture bursty realistic workloads; relies on synthetic SMOOTH mobility models rather than real trace variations.
full_citation: [1]S. Guan and A. Boukerche, âA Novel Mobility-Aware Offloading Management Scheme in Sustainable Multi-Access Edge Computing,â IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Computing, vol. 7, no. 1, pp. 1â13, Jan. 2022, doi: 10.1109/tsusc.2021.3065310.

Title: A Probabilistic VDTN Routing Scheme Based on Hybrid Swarm-Based Approach
authors: Youcef Azzoug, Abdelmadjid Boukra, Vasco N. G. J. Soares
network_environment: Vehicular Delay-Tolerant Networks (VDTNs) / sparse urban vehicular edge
swarm_algorithm: Hybrid Firefly Algorithm (FA) and Glowworm Swarm Optimization (GSO) with a 5-parameter fitness evaluation and METD-based geographic fallback
agent_characteristics: Distributed edge nodes (individual vehicles operating locally as firefly/glowworm agents evaluating 1-hop opportunistic neighbors)
operational_action: Opportunistic routing and next Store-Carry-and-Forward (SCF) relay vehicle selection
handling_of_disconnections: Store-Carry-and-Forward (SCF) mechanism where bundles remain in local vehicle buffers until an opportunistic contact with a higher fitness score or meeting METD recovery criteria is encountered
key_metrics_and_results: Evaluated using the ONE simulator (Helsinki city scenario) against PRoPHET and GeoSpray. limitations: Tested only in simulation with a relatively small network size (50 vehicles); relies on fixed equal weights for the fitness function parameters; assumes GPS/ETA availability for the recovery mechanism

Title: A Region Division-Based Adaptive Task Offloading in Collaborative LEO Heterogeneous Constellation
authors: Liang Zhao, Minglin Zeng, Ammar Hawbani, Yunhe Sun, Lexi Xu, Zhi Liu, Xiaoming Zhou
network_environment: Collaborative Low Earth Orbit (LEO) heterogeneous satellite constellation (Satellite Edge Computing)

Title: Bi-Objective Ant Colony Optimization for Trajectory Planning and Task Offloading in UAV-Assisted MEC Systems
authors: Yiqian Wang, Jie Zhu, Haiping Huang, Fu Xiao
network_environment: UAV-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) network with intermittently visited ground smart devices and base stations for battery swapping
swarm_algorithm: Bi-criterion Ant Colony Optimization (bi-ACO) incorporating multiple heterogeneous colonies, Feasible Solution Generation Method (FSGM), Solution Division Method (SDM), and Pheromone Update Method (PUM)
agent_characteristics: Centralized execution on an edge server that computes schedules and trajectories, then dispatches them to UAV agents via remote control
operational_action: Joint multi-UAV trajectory planning and multi-stage task offloading scheduling (data upload, computation, result return, and battery swap scheduling)
handling_of_disconnections: Employs an asynchronous store-carry-compute-and-forward model where UAVs visit ground devices to fetch data, process while flying/hovering, and revisit to return results within deadlines
